name: Abdurrahman Bala Bako
feedback: D1 is the strongest part of this submission. You catalogued all ten vulnerabilities plus the decoy, and almost every finding carries a quoted code line or a capture timestamp, which is exactly what earns full credit. SQL injection in 01-legacy-admin-login.php is nailed with the string-concat WHERE clause and the admin' OR '1'='1 payload tied to 02:15:31, stored XSS is tied to the cookie beacon at 02:18:47, path traversal shows the root:x:0:0 response at 02:24:02, and the XXE entity is quoted. A few CWE numbers drifted, MD5 as CWE-327 rather than CWE-916, alg:none as CWE-345 rather than CWE-347, and the cookie flags as CWE-1004 rather than CWE-614, and XXE was filed under A03 rather than A05, all of which are defensible class variants so I did not punish them hard. Your decoy handling is correct and the reason I held D1 high: you named hash_equals as the tempting safe construct, proved it safe because constant-time comparison defeats timing attacks, and correctly kept alg:none as a real bug rather than calling it the decoy, which is the trap many candidates fall into. D2 reconciles the chain hop by hop with timestamps and verbatim payloads, which is good, but the CVSS work let you down on the flagship finding. You scored SQL injection 10.0 with S:C and A:H, and the defensible vector here is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at roughly 9.1, because an auth bypass does not touch availability and does not change scope at that hop, so revisit A:N and S:U there. Your impact section names 312 customers and the 6,400 to 950,000 NGN balance range and honestly states that no live testing was done, but you stopped short of summing the exposure into a tens-of-millions naira figure and you never connected it to BoltCash or to the forged super_admin token reaching the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is the senior scope-change insight that would have lifted this row. D3 reads cleanly, ties findings to artefacts, states the decoy correctly, and names SQL injection as the single earliest-break fix, all of which I credited. Two things held it back: your remediation is ordered by risk-reduction and impact rather than by effort-to-risk, which is the ordering the brief asked for, and your two detection stopgaps name log patterns but give no false-positive rates, so an operator cannot judge the noise, add an exact field and an FP estimate for each. D4 is in a strong personal voice and is anchored to your own findings, but it only answers two of the four prompts cleanly, the what-goes-in-writing prompt and the one-non-negotiable-action prompt are not clearly resolved, you cite ISC2 Canon I and II by number which is good, but you never name the NDPA 2023 breach duty, so add section 40 for the 72-hour NDPC notification and section 41 for notifying the 312 affected data subjects on high risk. No fabrication was present, every evidence line traces to the pack. The single most important fix is to correct the SQL injection CVSS vector to S:U and A:N around 9.1 and to justify each metric in one sentence, because a wrong score on your top finding undermines the whole risk story.
